# Pediatric AML Target Discovery
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Screen the surfaceome for marrow-sparing immunotherapy targets, then profile
# any candidate for efficacy, safety, cross-cohort validation and combinations.
# Driven entirely by the manuscript Source Data in ../source_data \u2014 no .h5ad.
#
#   shiny::runApp("app")          # from the repository root
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

library(shiny); library(bslib); library(ggplot2); library(DT)

# Data arrives as one binary bundle (app/prep_bundle.R). Reading 24 MB of CSV at
# startup was what left the browser on a spinner; the bundle is 2 MB and R
# deserialises it instead of parsing it. Falling back to the raw CSVs keeps the
# app runnable straight from the repository during development.
B <- local({
  for (p in c("bundle.rds", file.path("app", "bundle.rds"), file.path("..", "bundle.rds")))
    if (file.exists(p)) return(readRDS(p))
  prep <- Filter(file.exists, c("prep_bundle.R", file.path("app", "prep_bundle.R")))
  data <- Filter(dir.exists, c("source_data", file.path("..", "source_data"),
                               file.path(dirname(getwd()), "source_data")))
  if (length(prep) && length(data)) { source(prep[1], local = TRUE); return(build_bundle(data[1])) }
  stop("no bundle.rds and no source_data/ - run Rscript app/prep_bundle.R first")
})
# Two antigens arrive under two names. IL3RA is CD123 and CLEC12A is CLL-1: the
# screen-side tables use the gene symbol, while the per-state, cytogenetic and
# combination tables use the CD name, and no table uses both. Selecting one name
# therefore left every panel keyed to the other reporting no data when the data
# was there under its other name. Normalise to the HGNC symbol, which is also
# what the CELLxGENE, Protein Atlas and GTEx links need.
ALIAS <- c(CD123 = "IL3RA", `CLL-1` = "CLEC12A")
.unalias <- function(x) { i <- match(as.character(x), names(ALIAS))
                          ifelse(is.na(i), as.character(x), unname(ALIAS[i])) }
for (.nm in names(B)) if (is.data.frame(B[[.nm]])) {
  for (.cl in intersect(c("gene", "label", "g1", "g2"), names(B[[.nm]])))
    B[[.nm]][[.cl]] <- .unalias(B[[.nm]][[.cl]])
  if ("combo" %in% names(B[[.nm]])) {          # strings like "CD123 OR CD33"
    .v <- as.character(B[[.nm]]$combo)
    for (.a in names(ALIAS)) .v <- gsub(paste0("\\b", .a, "\\b"), ALIAS[[.a]], .v, perl = TRUE)
    B[[.nm]]$combo <- .v
  }
}

screen <- B$screen; funnel <- B$funnel; h2h <- B$h2h; ls_expr <- B$ls_expr
cyto <- B$cyto; meta_ped <- B$meta_ped; meta_ad <- B$meta_ad; sc_ad <- B$sc_ad
radar <- B$radar; tox_hema <- B$tox_hema; tox_org <- B$tox_org; combos <- B$combos
tox_ct <- B$tox_ct
lsspec <- B$lsspec; lscomp <- B$lscomp; emb <- B$emb; ebins <- B$ebins
# Counted from the atlas, not typed: the pooled healthy-donor marrows are not
# patients, and the state levels are whatever states the bundle actually holds.
N_PT <- sum(!grepl("^0_Healthy", unique(as.character(emb$sample))))
LS_LEVELS <- paste0("LS_", sort(as.integer(sub("^LS_", "",
                      unique(as.character(emb$LS)[nzchar(as.character(emb$LS))])))))

# expression: dense uint8 matrix [bin, gene], so a gene lookup is a column read
GMAT <- B$gmat; GSCALE <- B$gmax / 255
EXPR_GENES <- B$genes_mapped

# The matrix above covers the 1,317 genes the screen was exported for. The atlas
# itself quantifies 21,895, and the rest are reachable too: inlining all of them
# would add 45 MB of base64 for the browser to parse before the app starts, so
# they ship as 343 files beside the app and one is fetched the first time a gene
# in it is picked. Each file is 64 genes and about 147 KB, and is kept for the
# rest of the session. Genes are sorted, so position in ALL_GENES gives the file.
# Named in two places, and they must agree: R hands this scope to the browser.
ALL_SCOPE <- "Any gene in the atlas"
ALL_GENES <- B$all_genes
ALL_SCALE <- B$all_gmax / 255
CHUNK_N   <- B$chunk_size
# webR has no libcurl -- capabilities("libcurl") is FALSE -- and download.file()
# resolves a relative URL against the worker script under /shinylive/ rather than
# against the app page, so only a root-absolute or fully qualified URL fetches.
# The page the app is served from is the authority when it reaches us; this is
# the fallback, and build.py asserts the directory it names still exists.
APP_BASE <- "/aml-atlas/"
.cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())

# Two directories ship beside the app and are read a file at a time: genes/ for
# the 21,895-gene expression matrix, cellchat/ for the per-group interaction
# tables. Whatever is fetched is kept for the rest of the session.
fetch_rds <- function(rel) {
  if (!is.null(.cache[[rel]])) return(.cache[[rel]])
  dest <- file.path(tempdir(), gsub("/", "_", rel))
  for (base in unique(c(get0(".base", .cache), APP_BASE))) {
    got <- tryCatch({
      suppressWarnings(utils::download.file(paste0(base, rel), dest,
                                            mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE))
      if (file.exists(dest) && file.size(dest) > 0L) readRDS(dest) else NULL
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(got)) {
      assign(".base", base, .cache)
      .cache[[rel]] <- got
      return(got)
    }
  }
  NULL                                   # offline, or the files were not deployed
}

fetch_chunk <- function(ci) fetch_rds(sprintf("genes/g%03d.rds", ci))

gene_bins <- function(g) {
  i <- match(g, EXPR_GENES)
  if (!is.na(i)) return(as.integer(GMAT[, i]) * GSCALE)
  if (is.na(match(g, ALL_GENES))) return(NULL)
  m <- fetch_chunk((match(g, ALL_GENES) - 1L) %/% CHUNK_N)
  if (is.null(m) || !(g %in% colnames(m))) return(NULL)
  as.integer(m[, g]) * ALL_SCALE
}

# Each panel is measured on a different subset of genes. Rather than let someone
# pick a gene and hit an empty panel, the sidebar can narrow the picker to the
# genes a given panel actually covers.
SCOPES <- list(
  # First, and the default. Without it CD33, CD38, CLEC12A, IL3RA, FLT3 and
  # ABCA7 cannot be reached at all: they sit outside the screen, so the list the
  # picker opens on does not contain them under any name.
  "Every gene in this app"    = sort(unique(c(screen$gene, EXPR_GENES, h2h$gene,
                                              ls_expr$gene, cyto$gene, radar$gene,
                                              tox_hema$gene, tox_org$gene))),
  "Every screened gene"       = sort(unique(screen$gene)),
  "Mapped on the atlas"       = sort(unique(EXPR_GENES)),
  # Everything the atlas quantifies, not just the surfaceome the screen ran on.
  # Fetched a file at a time, so picking one of these costs a 147 KB download
  # once per 64 genes rather than anything at startup.
  "Any gene in the atlas"     = ALL_GENES,          # == ALL_SCOPE below
  "Head-to-head panel"        = sort(unique(h2h$gene)),
  "Profiled per leukemic state" = sort(unique(ls_expr$gene)),
  "Full safety and validation"  = sort(unique(radar$gene)))
SCOPE_LABELS <- sprintf("%s (%s)", names(SCOPES),
                        format(lengths(SCOPES), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE))
# Show "IL3RA (CD123)" while the value stays IL3RA, so either name finds it.
ALIAS_OF <- stats::setNames(names(ALIAS), unname(ALIAS))
gene_choices <- function(g) {
  lab <- g; i <- match(g, names(ALIAS_OF))
  lab[!is.na(i)] <- sprintf("%s (%s)", g[!is.na(i)], unname(ALIAS_OF[i[!is.na(i)]]))
  stats::setNames(g, lab)
}

PROG  <- c(favorable = "#2F5D70", poor = "#8C1515", n.s. = "#B9C0C7", normal = "#7E57C2")
# Lineage of each annotated cell type, for colouring the violins. The AML- prefix
# marks the sample a cell came from, not the compartment: only AML, AML-PCNA,
# AML-MKI67 and AML-CD1C are leukemic, and those four are exactly the 70,108
# leukemic cells. AML-Ery, AML-CD4T, AML-B and the rest are normal cells in an
# AML marrow, so they take the lineage colour of what they are.
# Names go through setNames rather than backticks: R rejects a \u escape inside
# backticks, and several of these annotations carry a diaeresis.
LINEAGE <- stats::setNames(
  c(rep("Leukemic", 4),
    rep("T cell", 7),
    rep("NK cell", 2),
    rep("B cell", 6),
    rep("Monocyte / DC", 6),
    rep("Erythroid", 2),
    rep("Progenitor", 2)),
  c("AML", "AML-PCNA", "AML-MKI67", "AML-CD1C",
    "Na\u00efve_CD4T", "CTL", "AML-CD4T", "Na\u00efve_CD8T", "AML-CTL",
      "Activated_CD4T", "AML-Na\u00efve_CD8T",
    "NK", "AML-NK",
    "CD20+B", "AML-B", "ProB", "PreB", "PlasmaB", "CD34+ProB",
    "CD14_Monocyte", "AML-CD14", "mDC", "CD16_Monocyte", "pDC", "Macrophage",
    "AML-Ery", "Erythrocytes",
    "Myeloid_Pro", "0_HSPC"))
LIN_COL <- c(Leukemic = "#8C1515", `T cell` = "#2F5D70", `NK cell` = "#4E9A86",
             `B cell` = "#7E57C2", `Monocyte / DC` = "#F6A30C", Erythroid = "#C2567A",
             Progenitor = "#8A8F98")
# --- microenvironment ------------------------------------------------------
# The T/NK compartment was clustered separately and carries the only per-cell
# surface-protein and TCR measurements in the study. Unlike the whole-marrow
# annotation, these cells carry the sample they came from, so AML marrow and
# healthy donor marrow can actually be told apart: the AML- prefix on a
# whole-marrow cell type is not a reliable marker of origin: 2,263 cells of
# lymphoid lineage sit in unprefixed whole-marrow types and still came from an
# AML sample (sum(lin %in% c("T cell","NK cell") & !grepl("^AML-", cell_type) &
# !grepl("^0_Healthy", sample)) over emb).
TNK <- B$tnk; TCR <- B$tcr
MK_LABEL <- stats::setNames(
  c("CD3", "CD7", "CD45RA", "CD127 (IL-7Rα)", "CD25 (IL-2Rα)",
    "CD279 (PD-1)", "CD152 (CTLA-4)", "CD366 (TIM-3)"),
  c("CD3_pos", "CD7_pos", "CD45RA_pos", "CD127_pos", "CD25_pos",
    "CD279_pos", "CD152_pos", "CD366_pos"))
MK_CHOICES <- stats::setNames(names(MK_LABEL), unname(MK_LABEL))
MARROW  <- stats::setNames(c("AML marrow", "Healthy donor marrow"), c("AML", "HBM"))
MAR_COL <- stats::setNames(c("#8C1515", "#2F5D70"), unname(MARROW))
marrow_f <- function(g) factor(unname(MARROW[as.character(g)]), levels = unname(MARROW))

# --- cell-cell communication -----------------------------------------------
# CellChat over all 75 groups: the 49 leukemic states, the leukemic cells whose
# cluster did not clear the Jaccard 0.35 stability cut, and the 25 annotated
# non-leukemic types. Of 4,165,145 ligand-receptor links, 933,682 reach p < 0.05
# by permutation and only those are kept. Totals per ordered pair are inlined
# here; the links behind them are one file per group, fetched when picked.
CC_GROUPS <- B$cc_groups
CC_PAIRS  <- B$cc_pairs
CC_CLASS <- function(x) {
  x <- as.character(x); out <- unname(LINEAGE[x])
  out[grepl("^LS_", x)] <- "Leukemic state"
  out[x == "AML (unassigned)"] <- "Leukemic, no state"
  out[is.na(out)] <- "Other"
  factor(out, levels = c("Leukemic state", "Leukemic, no state",
                         names(LIN_COL)[-1], "Other"))
}
CC_COL <- c(stats::setNames(c("#8C1515", "#C06A6A"),
                            c("Leukemic state", "Leukemic, no state")),
            LIN_COL[-1], stats::setNames("#B9C0C7", "Other"))
DE_ALL <- B$de_all    # leukemic vs normal, every one of the 21,895 atlas genes
LS_UP  <- B$ls_up     # per-state Wilcoxon, 8,289 genes over 48 states
TNK_DE <- B$tnk_de    # T/NK AML vs healthy donor, 7,689 genes over 12 subsets
CYTO_BULK <- B$cyto_bulk     # the 12 targets by cytogenetic subtype, both bulk cohorts
PT_LINS <- setdiff(names(LIN_COL), "Leukemic")
cc_file <- function(g) sprintf("cellchat/g%02d.rds", match(g, CC_GROUPS) - 1L)
CC_GENE_MAP <- B$cc_gene_map            # gene -> interaction, complexes expanded
CC_LEUK     <- B$cc_leuk                # 49 states + the unassigned leukemic cells
CC_NORMAL   <- B$cc_normal              # the annotated non-leukemic types

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Every number quoted in the prose below is computed here, from the bundle that
# is actually loaded, so that the text and the data cannot drift apart. Nothing
# in a note is a typed literal. Constants that are genuine choices rather than
# measurements (plot cuts, sampling caps, reporting gates) are named here too
# and referenced by both the code and the prose, so the two cannot disagree.
#
# Arbitrary, not derived from data:
#   TOP_N, ORG_TOPN, CT_TOPN, VIOL_DOTS_N, DE_BG_N, CC_TOPN  - display cuts and
#     sampling caps, chosen for legibility and WebAssembly draw speed.
#   LYMPH_GATE  - the purity threshold this app reports against.
# Upstream method parameters, fixed by the analysis, not by this app:
#   Jaccard 0.35 state-stability cut; the <=10% marrow-sparing gate; the 25-cell
#   detection floor for the map; CellChat's 100-cell per-group floor.
# External reference, not measurable here:
#   the CZ CELLxGENE Census tissue count ("roughly 65").
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOP_N       <- 500L   # arbitrary: rows in the safety browser
ORG_TOPN    <- 15L    # arbitrary: organs plotted on the Safety tab
CT_TOPN     <- 20L    # arbitrary: cell types plotted on the Organ check tab
VIOL_DOTS_N <- 400L   # arbitrary: cells overlaid per violin
DE_BG_N     <- 12000L # arbitrary: genes in the volcano backdrop
CC_TOPN     <- 500L   # arbitrary: links listed per group and direction
LYMPH_GATE  <- 90     # arbitrary: purity threshold reported for the T/NK bins
TME_MIN     <- 20L    # arbitrary: cells needed before a per-patient share is shown
PT_MIN      <- 100L   # arbitrary: non-leukemic cells needed before a marrow is shown

fm    <- function(x) format(as.integer(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
SPELL <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight",
           "nine", "ten", "eleven", "twelve")
spell <- function(n) if (n >= 1L && n <= length(SPELL)) SPELL[[n]] else fm(n)
Spell <- function(n) { s <- spell(n); paste0(toupper(substring(s, 1, 1)), substring(s, 2)) }
and_list <- function(x) if (length(x) < 2L) paste(x, collapse = "") else
  paste0(paste(utils::head(x, -1L), collapse = ", "), " and ", utils::tail(x, 1L))

NUM <- local({
  inLS  <- nzchar(as.character(emb$LS)) & !is.na(emb$LS)
  ctab  <- table(as.character(emb$cell_type))
  lstab <- table(as.character(emb$LS)[inLS])
  samp  <- unique(as.character(emb$sample))
  lin   <- unname(LINEAGE[as.character(emb$cell_type)])

  # group size for every CellChat group, on the same cells the atlas holds
  ccsz <- vapply(CC_GROUPS, function(g)
    if (grepl("^LS_", g)) as.integer(lstab[g])
    else if (identical(g, "AML (unassigned)")) sum(emb$compartment == "Leukemic" & !inLS)
    else as.integer(ctab[g]), integer(1))
  names(ccsz) <- CC_GROUPS

  # does incoming signal track group size? reported in the Partners note
  inc <- tapply(CC_PAIRS$strength, as.character(CC_PAIRS$target), sum)
  rho <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor(inc[CC_GROUPS], ccsz,
                                     method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"))

  # which groups actually survive into the state-by-cell-type grid
  seen   <- unique(c(as.character(CC_PAIRS$source), as.character(CC_PAIRS$target)))
  leuk_k <- intersect(CC_LEUK, seen)
  norm_k <- intersect(CC_NORMAL, seen)

  # purity of the atlas bins the separately clustered T/NK cells sit in
  isL <- lin %in% c("T cell", "NK cell")
  shr <- 100 * tapply(isL, as.character(emb$bin), mean)
  pure <- 100 * mean(shr[as.character(TNK$bin)] >= LYMPH_GATE, na.rm = TRUE)

  # the state with no per-state test, and how few cells put it there
  untested <- setdiff(names(lstab), unique(as.character(LS_UP$LS)))

  # bulk cytogenetic cohorts: one row per patient per gene, so rows / genes
  ngb <- length(unique(CYTO_BULK$gene))
  coh <- lapply(split(CYTO_BULK, as.character(CYTO_BULK$cohort)), function(s) {
    tb <- table(as.character(s$cyto)) / ngb
    tb <- sort(tb[tb > 0])
    list(n = sum(tb), k = length(tb), tb = tb)
  })

  # per-marrow immune compartment: which marrows clear the floor, and how much
  # of each shown marrow is non-leukemic at all
  nlc  <- table(as.character(emb$sample)[lin != "Leukemic"])
  tots <- table(as.character(emb$sample))
  shown_s <- names(nlc)[nlc >= PT_MIN]
  shr_s   <- 100 * as.numeric(nlc[shown_s]) / as.numeric(tots[shown_s])

  # the deep-profiled twelve against the marrow ranking
  top_deep <- screen$gene[order(screen$rank)][seq_len(nrow(radar))]
  noorg    <- setdiff(top_deep, unique(as.character(tox_org$gene)))

  list(
    cells = nrow(emb), leuk = sum(emb$compartment == "Leukemic"),
    norm = sum(emb$compartment != "Leukemic"), ctypes = length(ctab),
    in_state = sum(inLS), n_states = length(lstab),
    unassigned = sum(emb$compartment == "Leukemic" & !inLS),
    ct_min = min(ctab), ct_max = max(ctab),
    patients = sum(!grepl("^0_Healthy", samp)), samp_tot = ctab[0],
    tnk = nrow(TNK), tcr = nrow(TCR), tcr_expanded = sum(TCR$expanded),
    screened = nrow(screen),
    funnel_mye = funnel$n[grep("Myeloid-sparing", funnel$stage)[1]],
    h2h = nrow(h2h), deep = nrow(radar), axes = ncol(radar) - 3L,
    only19 = length(unique(as.character(ls_expr$gene))),
    census_ct = length(unique(as.character(tox_ct$cell_type))),
    census_org = length(unique(as.character(tox_org$organ))),
    atlas_genes = length(ALL_GENES),
    tnkde_genes = length(unique(as.character(TNK_DE$gene))),
    tnkde_sub = length(unique(as.character(TNK_DE$subset))),
    lsup_genes = length(unique(as.character(LS_UP$gene))),
    lsup_states = length(unique(as.character(LS_UP$LS))),
    untested = untested, untested_n = sum(as.character(emb$LS) %in% untested),
    cc_groups = length(CC_GROUPS), cc_states = sum(grepl("^LS_", CC_GROUPS)),
    cc_rho = rho, cc_big_norm = names(which.max(ccsz[CC_NORMAL])),
    grid_leuk = length(leuk_k), grid_norm = length(norm_k),
    grid_leuk_all = length(CC_LEUK), grid_norm_all = length(CC_NORMAL),
    grid_dropped = c(setdiff(CC_LEUK, leuk_k), setdiff(CC_NORMAL, norm_k)),
    lymph_pure = pure, coh = coh, noorg = noorg,
    pt_shown = length(shown_s), pt_below = sum(nlc < PT_MIN),
    pt_lo = min(shr_s), pt_hi = max(shr_s)
  )
})


# Circos-style network, the shape CellChat's own netVisual_circle draws and the
# one Figure 7E uses: groups sit on a circle and a curved directed edge carries
# the summed probability between them. Drawn in base R + ggplot2 so the app
# needs no extra package; circlize exists for webR but pulls 6.4 MB into every
# boot of every browser, and the runtime fetches all packages eagerly.
.edge <- function(p0, p1, n = 60, bend = 0.45) {
  # single control point pulled toward the centre, so edges bow inward and
  # reciprocal pairs separate instead of overprinting
  m <- (p0 + p1) / 2
  ctl <- m * bend
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)
  data.frame(x = (1-t)^2*p0[1] + 2*(1-t)*t*ctl[1] + t^2*p1[1],
             y = (1-t)^2*p0[2] + 2*(1-t)*t*ctl[2] + t^2*p1[2])
}
.rot <- function(p, a) c(p[1]*cos(a) - p[2]*sin(a), p[1]*sin(a) + p[2]*cos(a))

circos_plot <- function(d, focal, focal_n, cols) {
  d <- d[order(-(d$out + d$inn)), ]
  n <- nrow(d)
  if (!n) return(NULL)
  # focal at the top, partners clockwise
  ang <- pi/2 - seq(0, 2*pi, length.out = n + 2)[-(n + 2)]
  nodes <- data.frame(
    grp  = c(focal, d$partner),
    cls  = c("focal", as.character(d$cls)),
    size = c(focal_n, d$n_cells),
    a    = ang)
  nodes$x <- cos(nodes$a); nodes$y <- sin(nodes$a)

  segs <- list()
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    p0 <- c(nodes$x[1], nodes$y[1]); p1 <- c(nodes$x[i + 1], nodes$y[i + 1])
    if (d$out[i] > 0) segs[[length(segs) + 1]] <-
      cbind(.edge(p0 * .93, p1 * .93, bend = .5),
            id = paste0("o", i), dir = "sends", w = d$out[i])
    if (d$inn[i] > 0) segs[[length(segs) + 1]] <-
      cbind(.edge(p1 * .93, p0 * .93, bend = .28),
            id = paste0("i", i), dir = "receives", w = d$inn[i])
  }
  E <- do.call(rbind, segs)
  nodes$hj <- ifelse(nodes$x < -0.05, 1, ifelse(nodes$x > 0.05, 0, 0.5))
  nodes$lx <- nodes$x * 1.17; nodes$ly <- nodes$y * 1.17

  ggplot() +
    geom_path(data = E, aes(x, y, group = id, colour = dir, linewidth = w),
              alpha = .7, lineend = "round",
              arrow = arrow(length = grid::unit(0.16, "cm"), type = "closed")) +
    geom_point(data = nodes, aes(x, y, fill = cls, size = size),
               shape = 21, colour = "white", stroke = 1.1) +
    geom_text(data = nodes, aes(lx, ly, label = grp, hjust = hj), size = 4.2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(sends = "#8C1515", receives = "#2F5D70"),
                        name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_linewidth(range = c(.35, 3.4), guide = "none") +
    scale_size(range = c(3.5, 13), guide = "none") +
    # asymmetric x: the right-hand labels are the long ones, so give them the
    # room rather than padding both sides and shrinking the circle
    coord_equal(xlim = c(-1.45, 1.85), ylim = c(-1.3, 1.3), clip = "off") +
    theme_void(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 13))
}

CC_SIZE <- stats::setNames(as.list(as.integer(table(
  c(ifelse(as.character(emb$cell_type) %in% c("AML","AML-PCNA","AML-MKI67","AML-CD1C"),
           ifelse(nzchar(as.character(emb$LS)), as.character(emb$LS), "AML (unassigned)"),
           as.character(emb$cell_type))))[CC_GROUPS])), CC_GROUPS)

KLASS <- c(lead = "#8C1515", candidate = "#2F5D70", clinical = "#F6A30C",
           control = "#7E57C2", ppac = "#5B8C5A")
CARD  <- "#8C1515"; TEAL <- "#2F5D70"

theme_lab <- function(rot = 45) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
          axis.text.x = element_text(angle = rot, hjust = if (rot > 0) 1 else .5))
}
note <- function(...) div(class = "text-muted", style = "font-size:.85rem;margin-top:.5rem", ...)
ext  <- function(label, url) a(label, href = url, target = "_blank", rel = "noopener",
                               style = "font-weight:600")
gene_links <- function(g) tagList(

# --- server ----------------------------------------------------------------
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # Where the app is actually served from, so the gene files are found whatever
  # path the site is mounted at. Same origin, so the parent location is readable.
  observeEvent(input$page_base, {
    if (is.character(input$page_base) && nzchar(input$page_base))
      assign(".base", input$page_base, .cache)
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE, once = TRUE)

  g <- reactive(if (is.null(input$gene) || !nzchar(input$gene)) "CD96" else input$gene)

  # narrowing the list keeps the current gene when that gene is in the new list
  observeEvent(input$glist, {
    ch  <- SCOPES[[input$glist]]; cur <- isolate(input$gene)
    # The all-atlas list is swapped in the browser, not here. Two measurements
    # drove that: updateSelectizeInput renders one <option> tag per choice in R,
    # which costs 16.3s for 21,895 of them in WebAssembly, while selectize loads
    # the same list in 18ms. server = TRUE is worse again -- it sends every
    # keystroke to a single-threaded R worker that is also drawing the plots, and
    # the search never saw past the first 200 symbols, so no gene could be found.
    # R still receives the chosen gene through input$gene as usual.
    if (identical(input$glist, ALL_SCOPE)) return(invisible(NULL))
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "gene", choices = gene_choices(ch),
                         selected = if (!is.null(cur) && cur %in% ch) cur else ch[1])
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  # what this study actually measured for the selected gene
  has_map  <- reactive(g() %in% EXPR_GENES || g() %in% ALL_GENES)
  has_ls   <- reactive(has(ls_expr,  g()))
  has_cyto <- reactive(has(cyto,     g()))
  has_h2h  <- reactive(has(h2h,      g()))
  has_tox  <- reactive(has(tox_hema, g()))
  has_org  <- reactive(has(tox_org,  g()))
  has_ct   <- reactive(has(tox_ct,   g()))
  has_rad  <- reactive(has(radar,    g()))
  has_val  <- reactive(has(meta_ped, g()) || has(meta_ad, g()) || has(sc_ad, g()))
  has_cmb  <- reactive(any(combos$g1 == g() | combos$g2 == g()))

  ONLY19 <- sprintf("Only the %d antigens taken forward from the screen were profiled this way.", NUM$only19)
  ONLY12 <- sprintf("Deep Census profiling was run on the %s antigens carried past the screen.", spell(NUM$deep))

  # A gene with no data for a panel gets the note alone - not a note above an
  # empty 400px canvas, which reads as a failure rather than as "not measured".
  slot <- function(ok, miss, id, h) if (ok) plotOutput(id, height = h) else miss
  output$ls_slot    <- renderUI(slot(has_ls(),   uiOutput("ls_miss"),    "ls_plot",    380))
  output$cyto_slot  <- renderUI(slot(has_cyto(), uiOutput("cyto_miss"),  "cyto_plot",  330))
  output$hema_slot  <- renderUI(slot(has_tox(),  uiOutput("hema_miss"),  "hema_plot",  400))
  output$org_slot   <- renderUI(slot(has_org(),  uiOutput("org_miss"),   "org_plot",   400))
  output$radar_slot <- renderUI(slot(has_rad(),  uiOutput("radar_miss"), "radar_plot", 300))
  output$valid_slot <- renderUI(slot(has_val(),  uiOutput("valid_miss"), "valid_plot", 420))

  output$ls_miss    <- renderUI(if (!has_ls())   elsewhere(g(), "per-state expression", ONLY19))
  output$cyto_miss  <- renderUI(if (!has_cyto()) elsewhere(g(), "cytogenetic breakdown", ONLY19))
  output$hema_miss  <- renderUI(if (!has_tox())  elsewhere(g(), "normal-marrow cell-type profile", ONLY12))
  output$org_miss   <- renderUI(if (!has_org())  elsewhere(g(), "vital-organ profile", ONLY12))
  output$radar_miss <- renderUI(if (!has_rad())  elsewhere(g(), "five-axis profile", ONLY12))
  output$valid_miss <- renderUI(if (!has_val())  elsewhere(g(), "cross-cohort validation", ONLY12))

  # Expression by cytogenetic subtype in the two bulk cohorts. Measured for the
  # same twelve targets as the other 12-gene panels, so a gene outside that set
  # gets the usual pointer rather than an empty frame.
  # unique(), not levels(): the alias pass at load rewrites every "gene" column
  # through .unalias(), which returns character, so the factor levels are gone by
  # the time this runs and levels() would be NULL for every gene.
  has_cytob <- reactive(g() %in% unique(CYTO_BULK$gene))
  output$cytob_miss <- renderUI(
    if (!has_cytob()) elsewhere(g(), "bulk cytogenetic breakdown", ONLY12))
  output$cytob_title <- renderText(
    sprintf("%s across cytogenetic subtypes, in both bulk cohorts", g()))

  output$cytob_plot <- renderPlot({
    req(has_cytob())
    d <- CYTO_BULK[CYTO_BULK$gene == g(), ]
    validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No bulk cytogenetic data for this gene."))

  # --- Microenvironment ------------------------------------------------------
  # These cells carry no expression of their own: the per-cell measurements here

  tnk_expr <- reactive({

  # Share within each marrow, so the two are comparable although the AML side

  output$tme_phen_note <- renderUI(

  output$tde_note <- renderUI({
    d <- tde()

  # --- immune compartment per patient ----------------------------------------
  # Every non-leukemic cell in the atlas, grouped by lineage and by the sample it
  # came from. This is the whole immune compartment, not only the T/NK cells
  # above, and it is keyed on the sample label rather than on the cell-type name:
  # the AML- prefix does not mark origin: 5,456 unprefixed, non-leukemic cells
  # come from AML samples and 637 cells annotated leukemic come from healthy
  # donors. Both are counts over emb, re-derivable from the bundle.
  pt_tbl <- reactive({
    ct <- as.character(emb$cell_type)
    lin <- unname(LINEAGE[ct])
    nl <- !is.na(lin) & lin != "Leukemic"
    d <- data.frame(sample = as.character(emb$sample[nl]),
                    marrow = emb$marrow[nl],
                    lin = factor(lin[nl], levels = setdiff(names(LIN_COL), "Leukemic")),
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    keep <- names(which(table(d$sample) >= PT_MIN))
    d <- d[d$sample %in% keep, ]
    d
  })

    d <- pt_tbl()
    tb <- table(d$sample, d$lin)
    pc <- 100 * tb / rowSums(tb)
    z <- as.data.frame(as.table(pc), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    names(z) <- c("sample", "lin", "pct")
    z$lin <- factor(z$lin, levels = levels(d$lin))
    z$marrow <- d$marrow[match(z$sample, d$sample)]
    z$n <- as.integer(rowSums(tb)[z$sample])
    z
  })

  output$pt_plot <- renderPlot({
    z <- pt_share()
    validate(need(nrow(z) > 0, "No sample has enough non-leukemic cells."))
    if (identical(input$pt_view, "one")) {
      L <- if (is.null(input$pt_lin)) levels(z$lin)[1] else input$pt_lin
      d <- z[as.character(z$lin) == L, ]

        scale_colour_manual(values = MAR_COL, guide = "none") +

      tshare <- z$pct[as.character(z$lin) == "T cell"]
      names(tshare) <- z$sample[as.character(z$lin) == "T cell"]
      ord <- unique(z$sample)
      amls <- ord[z$marrow[match(ord, z$sample)] == "AML marrow"]
      hbm  <- setdiff(ord, amls)
      lv <- c(amls[order(-tshare[amls])], hbm)
      z$sample <- factor(z$sample, levels = lv)
      ggplot(z, aes(sample, pct, fill = lin)) +
        geom_col(width = .82) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = LIN_COL[levels(z$lin)], name = NULL) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "% of that marrow's non-leukemic cells") +
        theme_lab(45) +
        theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 11), axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
    }
  })

  output$pt_note <- renderUI({
    z <- pt_share()
    ns <- length(unique(z$sample))
    nh <- length(unique(z$sample[z$marrow == "Healthy donor marrow"]))
    note(sprintf("%d samples carry at least %d non-leukemic cells and are shown: %d with AML and %d healthy donors. ",
                 ns, PT_MIN, ns - nh, nh),
         sprintf("%s samples fall below that and are left out, because a composition from a few dozen cells ",
                 Spell(NUM$pt_below)),
         "moves by tens of percent on one cell. Shares are within each marrow's non-leukemic cells, ",
         "so they say what the immune compartment is made of and not how much of it there is: ",
         sprintf("that varies enormously, from %.1f%% of one marrow to %.0f%%. ", NUM$pt_lo, NUM$pt_hi),
         "Samples are keyed on the sample label, not on the cell-type name, because the AML- prefix ",
         "is not a reliable marker of which sample a cell came from.")
  })

  # --- Cell talk -------------------------------------------------------------
  cc_g <- reactive(if (is.null(input$cc_group) || !nzchar(input$cc_group))
                     CC_GROUPS[1] else input$cc_group)
  cc_out <- reactive(!identical(input$cc_dir, "in"))
  # Which partners to rank. Communication probability rises with the number of
  # cells in a group (Spearman 0.70 against group size here), and 49 of the 75
  # groups are leukemic states, so an unrestricted top 15 is almost all states
  # plus CD14_Monocyte, the largest immune group at 4,146 cells. For most states
  # that made monocytes look like the only immune partner. This narrows the
  # ranking without changing any number in it.
  cc_set <- reactive({
    switch(if (is.null(input$cc_set)) "all" else input$cc_set,
           normal = CC_NORMAL, leuk = CC_LEUK, CC_GROUPS)
  })

  # Which interactions the gene chosen in the sidebar takes part in, as ligand
  # or as any subunit of a receptor complex. Most genes are in none: CellChatDB
  # covers 1,383 genes, 975 of which the atlas also quantifies, against 21,895
  # genes in the picker.
  cc_hits <- reactive(CC_GENE_MAP$interaction_name[CC_GENE_MAP$gene == g()])
  cc_bygene <- reactive(isTRUE(input$cc_bygene))

  output$cc_gene_state <- renderUI({
    n <- length(cc_hits())
    if (n > 0)
      div(class = "text-muted", style = "font-size:.85rem",
          sprintf("%s is in %d interaction%s", g(), n, if (n == 1) "" else "s"))
    else
      div(class = "text-muted", style = "font-size:.85rem",
          sprintf("%s is not a ligand or receptor in CellChatDB, so it carries no interactions.", g()))
  })

  # Fetched once per group and kept; about 325 KB a group.
  cc_raw <- reactive(fetch_rds(cc_file(cc_g())))

  cc_links <- reactive({
    f <- cc_raw(); if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
    if (cc_bygene()) {
      if (!length(cc_hits())) return(f[0, ])
      f <- f[f$name %in% cc_hits(), ]
    }
    # Self-signalling is excluded here as well as in the partner views. It used
    # to be kept only here, so the pathway totals and the table included traffic
    # the circos and the bars did not -- 6.4% of the outgoing signal for
    # AML (unassigned) -- and the table listed sender-equals-receiver rows that
    # appeared nowhere else on the tab.
    keep <- cc_set()
    if (cc_out()) f[f$source == cc_g() & f$target != cc_g() & f$target %in% keep, ]
    else          f[f$target == cc_g() & f$source != cc_g() & f$source %in% keep, ]
  })

  # Partner strengths. Unfiltered these come from the inlined pair table, which
  # needs no download; filtered to one gene they have to be recomputed from the
  # group's own links, since the pair table is already summed over interactions.
  cc_two_way <- reactive({
    g0 <- cc_g()
    if (cc_bygene() && !length(cc_hits())) return(NULL)
    if (!cc_bygene()) {
      pr <- setdiff(union(as.character(CC_PAIRS$target[CC_PAIRS$source == g0]),
                          as.character(CC_PAIRS$source[CC_PAIRS$target == g0])), g0)
      if (!length(pr)) return(NULL)
      key <- paste(CC_PAIRS$source, CC_PAIRS$target)
      d <- data.frame(partner = pr,
                      out = CC_PAIRS$strength[match(paste(g0, pr), key)],
                      inn = CC_PAIRS$strength[match(paste(pr, g0), key)],
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    } else {
      f <- cc_raw(); if (is.null(f)) return(NULL)
      f <- f[f$name %in% cc_hits(), ]
      if (!nrow(f)) return(NULL)
      o <- f[f$source == g0 & f$target != g0, ]
      i <- f[f$target == g0 & f$source != g0, ]
      pr <- union(as.character(o$target), as.character(i$source))
      if (!length(pr)) return(NULL)
      so <- tapply(o$prob, factor(as.character(o$target), levels = pr), sum)
      si <- tapply(i$prob, factor(as.character(i$source), levels = pr), sum)
      d <- data.frame(partner = pr, out = as.numeric(so), inn = as.numeric(si),
                      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
    d$out[is.na(d$out)] <- 0; d$inn[is.na(d$inn)] <- 0
    d <- d[(d$out + d$inn) > 0 & d$partner %in% cc_set(), ]
    if (!nrow(d)) return(NULL)
    d$cls <- CC_CLASS(d$partner)
    d$n_cells <- unlist(CC_SIZE[d$partner])
    d[order(-(d$out + d$inn)), ]
  })

  cc_n <- reactive(if (is.null(input$cc_top)) 15L else as.integer(input$cc_top))

  output$cc_title <- renderText(
    sprintf("%s — %s (%s cells)%s", cc_g(),
            if (cc_out()) "who it signals to" else "who signals to it",
            format(CC_SIZE[[cc_g()]], big.mark = ","),
            if (cc_bygene() && length(cc_hits())) paste0(", through ", g()) else ""))

  output$cc_partners <- renderPlot({
    d <- cc_two_way()
    validate(need(!is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0,
                  if (isTRUE(input$cc_bygene) && length(cc_hits()) == 0)
                    paste0(g(), " is not a ligand or receptor in CellChatDB. ",
                           "Clear the gene filter, or pick a gene that is.")
                  else if (isTRUE(input$cc_bygene))
                    paste0("No significant ", g(), " interaction involves this group.")
                  else "No significant interactions for this group."))
    if (identical(input$cc_view, "bar")) {
      # ranked by the direction chosen, then cut -- not cut on combined traffic
      # first, which silently dropped partners that belong in this direction
      d$val <- if (cc_out()) d$out else d$inn
      d <- d[d$val > 0, ]
      validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No significant interactions in this direction."))
      d <- head(d[order(-d$val), ], cc_n())
      d$partner <- factor(d$partner, levels = rev(d$partner))
      ggplot(d, aes(partner, val, fill = cls)) +
        geom_col(width = .75) + coord_flip() +
        scale_fill_manual(values = CC_COL, drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
        labs(x = NULL, y = "Summed probability over significant links") +
        theme_lab(0) +
        theme(legend.position = "top", legend.text = element_text(size = 12),
              axis.text = element_text(size = 13), axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
    } else {
      p <- circos_plot(head(d, cc_n()), cc_g(), CC_SIZE[[cc_g()]],
                       c(CC_COL, stats::setNames("#111111", "focal")))
      validate(need(!is.null(p), "No significant interactions for this group."))
      p
    }
  })

  output$cc_note <- renderUI({
    gf <- if (cc_bygene() && length(cc_hits()))
      list(" Restricted to interactions involving ", strong(g()), ".") else NULL
    if (!identical(input$cc_view, "bar"))
      note("Every group that exchanges a significant signal with ", strong(cc_g()),
           ", the strongest first. A red arrow is a signal ", strong(cc_g()), " sends, a ",
           "blue arrow one it receives, and arrow thickness is the summed probability of the ",
           "significant ligand-receptor links behind it. Node size is the number of cells in ",
           "the group. Both directions are drawn at once here, so the Direction control above ",
           "applies to the ranked bars and to the two cards below, not to this view. ",
           "Self-signalling is left out.", gf)
    else
      note("Each bar is one partner group, summing the probability of every significant ",
           "ligand-receptor link between it and ", strong(cc_g()), " in the direction chosen. ",
           "Leukemic states are red, the normal compartments take their lineage colour. ",
           "Probability rises with the number of cells in a group as well as with expression, ",
           "so a large state outranking a small one is not by itself evidence that it signals ",
           "more per cell. That is why the Partners control exists: across these data the ",
           sprintf("incoming strength of a group tracks its size at Spearman %.2f, and with %d of the ",
                   NUM$cc_rho, NUM$cc_states),
           sprintf("%d groups leukemic, an unrestricted ranking is dominated by states and by ", NUM$cc_groups),
           sprintf("%s, the largest immune group. Restricting to the immune and normal ", NUM$cc_big_norm),
           "compartments ranks them against each other instead.", gf)
  })

  output$cc_miss <- renderUI(
    if (is.null(cc_raw()))
      div(class = "border rounded p-3", style = "background:#F7F8F9;font-size:.9rem",
          "The interaction detail for this group could not be loaded. The summary above ",
          "comes from data inside the app and is unaffected."))

  output$cc_paths <- renderPlot({
    d <- cc_links(); req(!is.null(d))
    validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No significant interactions in this direction."))
    z <- aggregate(d$prob, list(pathway = d$pathway), sum)
    names(z)[2] <- "strength"
    z <- head(z[order(-z$strength), ], 20)
    z$pathway <- factor(z$pathway, levels = rev(z$pathway))
    ggplot(z, aes(pathway, strength)) +
      geom_col(fill = TEAL, width = .75) + coord_flip() +
      labs(x = NULL, y = "Summed probability over significant links") +
      theme_lab(0) + theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 13),
                           axis.title = element_text(size = 13))
  })

  output$cc_tbl <- renderDT({
    d <- cc_links(); req(!is.null(d))
    validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No significant interactions in this direction."))
    z <- head(d[order(-d$prob), ], CC_TOPN)
    z <- data.frame(Sender = z$source, Receiver = z$target,
                    `Ligand-receptor` = z$name, Pathway = z$pathway,
                    Probability = z$prob, p = z$pval, check.names = FALSE)
    datatable(z, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none",
              options = list(pageLength = 10, order = list(list(4, "desc")))) |>
      formatSignif("Probability", 3)
  })

  # --- the whole atlas at once -----------------------------------------------
  output$cc_matrix <- renderPlot({
    states <- identical(input$cc_mat, "sn")
    d <- CC_PAIRS
    d$s <- as.character(d$source); d$t <- as.character(d$target)
    if (states) {
      out <- !identical(input$cc_mat_dir, "in")
      d <- if (out) d[d$s %in% CC_LEUK & d$t %in% CC_NORMAL, ]
           else      d[d$s %in% CC_NORMAL & d$t %in% CC_LEUK, ]
      validate(need(nrow(d) > 0, "No significant interactions."))
      d$row <- if (out) d$s else d$t
      d$col <- if (out) d$t else d$s
      ylab <- "Leukemic state"; xlab <- "Normal cell type"
    } else {
      d$row <- ifelse(d$s %in% CC_LEUK, "Leukemic (all states)", d$s)
      d$col <- ifelse(d$t %in% CC_LEUK, "Leukemic (all states)", d$t)
      d <- aggregate(list(strength = d$strength), list(row = d$row, col = d$col), sum)
      ylab <- "Sender"; xlab <- "Receiver"
    }
    ro <- names(sort(tapply(d$strength, d$row, sum), decreasing = FALSE))
    co <- names(sort(tapply(d$strength, d$col, sum), decreasing = TRUE))
    d$row <- factor(d$row, levels = ro); d$col <- factor(d$col, levels = co)
    ggplot(d, aes(col, row, fill = strength)) +
      geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = .4) +
      scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "rocket", direction = -1, trans = "sqrt",
                           name = "Summed\nprobability") +
      labs(x = xlab, y = ylab) +
      theme_lab(45) +
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
            axis.text = element_text(size = 11),
            axis.title = element_text(size = 13),
            legend.title = element_text(size = 12))
  })

  output$cc_mat_note <- renderUI(
    if (identical(input$cc_mat, "sn"))
      note("Every leukemic state against every normal cell type, in the direction chosen. ",
           "Each cell of the grid sums the probability of the significant ligand-receptor ",
           "links between that pair. Rows and columns are ordered by total, so the states ",
           sprintf("and the cell types that carry the most signal sit at the ends. The grid is %d ", NUM$grid_leuk),
           sprintf("states by %d cell types, not %d by %d: %s have no row or ",
                   NUM$grid_norm, NUM$grid_leuk_all, NUM$grid_norm_all, and_list(NUM$grid_dropped)),
           "column at all, because they fall under CellChat's 100-cell per-group floor and their ",
           "links were filtered out rather than tested and found absent.")
    else
      note(sprintf("All %d groups with the %d leukemic states and the unassigned leukemic cells ", NUM$cc_groups, NUM$cc_states),
           "summed into one row and column, so the normal compartments can be read against ",
           "each other and against the leukemia as a whole. ",
           strong("The leukemic total is a sum over states, not a separate CellChat run: "),
           "communication probability is not additive, so treat that row and column as an ",
           "indication of where the traffic is and not as a probability in its own right. ",
           "Every other cell of the grid is a single group pair and is exact."))

  # --- Organ check -----------------------------------------------------------
  # Marrow sparing is screened for all 1,704 genes; body-wide organ expression
  # only for the twelve carried past the screen. The two disagree sharply, so
  # this tab shows the dissociation and hands the reader the Census lookup for
  # every gene the study could not profile itself.
  CENSUS <- function(g) paste0("https://cellxgene.cziscience.com/gene-expression?genes=", g)

  output$tradeoff_plot <- renderPlot({
    d <- radar
    d$sel <- d$gene == g()
    ggplot(d, aes(Marrow_sparing, Organ_sparing)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 50, linetype = 2, colour = "#B9C0C7") +
      { if (any(d$sel)) geom_point(data = d[d$sel, ], size = 10, shape = 21, fill = NA,
                                   colour = "#F6A30C", stroke = 1.6) } +
      geom_point(aes(colour = group), size = 3.4) +
      geom_text(aes(label = label), vjust = -1.15, size = 3.2) +
      scale_colour_manual(values = KLASS, name = NULL) +
      labs(x = "Marrow sparing (score)", y = "Organ sparing (score)") +
      ylim(0, 112) + xlim(40, 104) + theme_lab(0)
  })

  output$organ_status_title <- renderText(sprintf("%s \u2014 organ status in this study", g()))

  output$organ_status <- renderUI({
    gg <- g()
    s  <- screen[screen$gene == gg, ]
    if (has_org()) {
      d <- tox_org[tox_org$gene == gg, ]
      d <- head(d[order(-d$pct), ], 5)
      r <- radar[radar$gene == gg, ]
      tagList(
        div(class = "alert alert-success py-2", style = "font-size:.9rem",
            strong("Profiled body-wide."), sprintf(" Organ-sparing score %.0f of 100.", r$Organ_sparing[1])),
        strong("Highest-expressing normal tissues"),
        tags$ul(lapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i)
          tags$li(sprintf("%s \u2014 %.1f%% of cells positive", d$organ[i], d$pct[i])))),
        if (has_ct()) {
          k <- tox_ct[tox_ct$gene == gg, ]
          k <- head(k[order(-k$pct), ], 5)
          tagList(
            strong("Highest-expressing normal cell types"),
            tags$ul(lapply(seq_len(nrow(k)), function(i)
              tags$li(sprintf("%s \u2014 %.1f%% of cells positive", k$cell_type[i], k$pct[i])))))
        },
        note("Every tissue and every cell type is listed below; the five-axis ",
             "panel is on the Safety tab.")
      )
    } else {
      tagList(
        div(class = "alert alert-warning py-2", style = "font-size:.9rem",
            strong("Not profiled body-wide here."),
            " Marrow sparing below is measured; organ expression is unknown in this study."),
        if (nrow(s)) tags$ul(
          tags$li(sprintf("Marrow rank %s of %s", s$rank[1], fm(NUM$screened))),
          tags$li(sprintf("%.1f%% of normal HSPC positive", s$scRNA_HSPC_pct[1])),
          tags$li(sprintf("%.1f%% of myeloid progenitors positive", s$scRNA_Myeloid_pct[1])),
          tags$li(sprintf("%.1f%% of leukemic cells positive", s$scRNA_AML_pct[1]))),
        note("Use the Census lookup on the right before treating this as a candidate.")
      )
    }
  })

  output$census_panel <- renderUI({
    gg <- g()
    tagList(
      div(style = "font-size:1.08rem;line-height:1.5;margin-bottom:.85rem",
          "The CZ CELLxGENE Census shows ", strong(gg), " across roughly 65 normal human ",
          "tissues, broken down by cell type, from millions of cells. Use it to see whether ",
          strong(gg), " is expressed anywhere an antigen-directed therapy would have to spare."),
      a(sprintf("Open %s in the CZ CELLxGENE Census \u2192", gg), href = CENSUS(gg),
        target = "_blank", rel = "noopener", class = "btn btn-primary btn-lg",
        style = "font-size:1.3rem;font-weight:700;padding:.75rem 1.4rem;white-space:normal"),
      div(style = "font-size:1.05rem;margin-top:.9rem",
          "Opens in a new tab. Also worth checking: ", gene_links(gg), "."),
      hr(),
      div(style = "font-size:1.05rem;font-weight:700", "What disqualifies a target"),
      tags$ul(style = "font-size:.98rem;margin-bottom:.4rem;line-height:1.5",
        tags$li("Appreciable expression on heart, brain, lung, liver, kidney or pancreas parenchyma \u2014 ",
                "the organs an antigen-directed therapy cannot spare."),
        tags$li("Expression on vascular endothelium, which carries the agent everywhere."),
        tags$li("Expression on normal HSPC or myeloid progenitors, which is the marrow axis the screen ",
                "already applies at a \u226410% gate."),
        tags$li("In this study CD9, IL1RAP and ABCA7 were disqualified on body-wide expression despite ",
                "passing the marrow gate.")),
      note("The Census is a cross-platform relative reference across roughly 65 tissues. It was not ",
           "statistically compared with the AML cohort in this study, and it is not a toxicology ",
           "prediction \u2014 it tells you where a transcript is detected in normal human tissue.")
    )
  })

  # The bundle carries all 54 tissues per profiled antigen; the Safety tab plots
  # only the top ORG_TOPN, which hid the rest. This shows every one, sortable, with
  # the cell count behind each percentage so a reader can weigh the evidence.
  VITAL <- c("heart", "brain", "central nervous system", "cortex", "spinal cord",
             "lung", "liver", "kidney", "pancreas", "vasculature", "eye",
             "respiratory system", "sensory system")

  output$organ_full_title <- renderText(
    if (has_org()) sprintf("%s across all %d normal tissues", g(), NUM$census_org)
    else sprintf("%s \u2014 no body-wide profile in this study", g()))

  output$organ_full_note <- renderUI(
    if (!has_org()) elsewhere(g(), "body-wide tissue profile", ONLY12))

  # The table and plot are declared statically in the UI: a DT nested inside a
  # renderUI on a tab that starts hidden initialises before Shiny binds its data
  # and renders "No matching records found".
  organ_full <- reactive({
    if (!has_org()) return(NULL)
    d <- tox_org[tox_org$gene == g(), c("organ", "pct", "mean", "n")]
    d[order(-d$pct), ]
  })

  output$organ_full_tbl <- renderDT({
    d <- organ_full()
    req(!is.null(d))
    d$vital <- ifelse(d$organ %in% VITAL, "vital", "")
    names(d) <- c("Tissue", "% positive", "Mean expr", "n cells", "Flag")
    datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none",
              options = list(pageLength = 12, order = list(list(1, "desc")))) |>
      formatRound("% positive", 1) |> formatRound("Mean expr", 3) |>
      formatRound("n cells", 0)
  })

  output$organ_full_plot <- renderPlot({
    d <- organ_full()
    req(!is.null(d))
    d$organ <- factor(d$organ, levels = rev(d$organ))
    d$vital <- d$organ %in% VITAL
    ggplot(d, aes(pct, organ, fill = vital)) +
      geom_col() +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = CARD, `FALSE` = "#B9C0C7"),
                        labels = c(`TRUE` = "vital organ", `FALSE` = "other tissue"),
                        name = NULL) +
      labs(x = "% of normal cells positive", y = NULL) +
      theme_lab(0) + theme(legend.position = "top")
  })

  output$ct_title <- renderText(
    if (has_ct()) sprintf("%s across all %d normal cell types", g(),
                          length(unique(tox_ct$cell_type)))
    else sprintf("%s \u2014 no cell-type profile in this study", g()))

  output$ct_tbl <- renderDT({
    req(has_ct())
    d <- tox_ct[tox_ct$gene == g(), c("cell_type", "pct", "mean", "n")]
    d <- d[order(-d$pct), ]
    names(d) <- c("Cell type", "% positive", "Mean expr", "n cells")
    datatable(d, rownames = FALSE, selection = "none",
              options = list(pageLength = 12, order = list(list(1, "desc")))) |>
      formatRound(2, 1) |> formatRound(3, 3)
  })

  output$ct_plot <- renderPlot({
    req(has_ct())
    d <- tox_ct[tox_ct$gene == g(), ]
    d <- head(d[order(-d$pct), ], CT_TOPN)
    d$cell_type <- factor(d$cell_type, levels = rev(d$cell_type))
    ggplot(d, aes(pct, cell_type)) +
      geom_col(fill = TEAL) +
      labs(x = "% of normal cells positive", y = NULL) +
      theme_lab(0)
  })

  output$organ_tbl <- renderDT({
    d <- screen[order(screen$rank),
                c("rank", "gene", "scRNA_AML_pct", "scRNA_HSPC_pct", "scRNA_Myeloid_pct")]
    d$organ <- ifelse(d$gene %in% radar$gene, "yes", "no")
    d$census <- sprintf('<a href="%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Census →</a>', CENSUS(d$gene))
    names(d) <- c("Marrow rank", "Gene", "% AML cells", "% HSPC", "% Myeloid",
                  "Organ screened", "Look up")
    datatable(d, selection = "single", rownames = FALSE, escape = FALSE,
              options = list(pageLength = 12, order = list(list(0, "asc")))) |>
      formatRound(c("% AML cells", "% HSPC", "% Myeloid"), 1)
  })
  observeEvent(input$organ_tbl_rows_selected, {
    d <- screen[order(screen$rank), ]
    updateSelectizeInput(session, "gene", selected = d$gene[input$organ_tbl_rows_selected])
  })
  outputOptions(output, "organ_full_tbl", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
}
